terms.title: Terms of
terms.lead: The rules for using Mediaory — in plain language. Please read the section on sources and content: it explains what we show, what we do not, and how publishers can reach us.

sections.title: About the service
body: Mediaory is a media and web monitoring service. It indexes publicly available sources and lets you search, track and report on mentions of the keywords you choose.

sections.title: Your account
body: Give us accurate information, keep your sign-in details safe, and tell us if you think your account was accessed without permission. You are responsible for activity under your account and for the people you invite to your organization.

sections.title: Sources and content
body: Mediaory is a search and indexing service for publicly available sources. For each result we show a headline, a short excerpt and a link to the original page. We do not republish articles — to read the full text you go to the publisher's own site.

All rights in the content we link to belong to its publishers and authors. Excerpts, reports and exports are provided for your organization's own monitoring and reporting; any further use is subject to the publisher's terms and applicable law.

Third-party content is provided as is. We are not responsible for its accuracy, completeness, timeliness or copyright status, and it may change or be removed at its source at any time. Sentiment labels, summaries and other AI-generated analysis are automated and can be wrong — check the original before you rely on it.
Publishers can ask us to stop indexing their site at any time using the takedown request form. We act on these requests promptly.

sections.title: Acceptable use
body: Do not use Mediaory unlawfully, to harass anyone, or to disrupt the service. Do not scrape, resell or redistribute the service or its data except as we agree in writing. Respect rate limits and the limits of your plan.

sections.title: Plans and fees
body: Where a paid plan is offered, its price, billing period and invoice details are shown before you buy. Invoices are issued to the company details you enter in your organization's billing profile.

sections.title: Availability and changes
body: We work to keep Mediaory available but do not promise uninterrupted service. We may change or retire features; we will give reasonable notice of changes that materially affect you.

sections.title: Liability
body: To the extent the law allows, Mediaory is not liable for indirect or consequential loss, or for decisions you make based on monitoring results. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law.

sections.title: Contact
body: Questions about these terms: use the contact page. Publishers: use the takedown request form.

bot.operatorName: Operated by {name}. Publisher requests reach our team through the opt-out form below.
bot.operatorContact: Configured crawler contact: {email}. This address is also sent in the HTTP From header.
bot.title: Meet
bot.lead: Mediaory-Bot is the crawler behind Mediaory, a media-monitoring service for businesses. This page explains what it does and how to ask it to stop.

sections.title: How it identifies itself
body: Every request carries this User-Agent: Mediaory-Bot/1.0 (+https://mediaory.io/bot). We do not disguise the crawler as a browser. Our requests come from cloud hosting and do not use a fixed IP address, so the User-Agent is the reliable way to recognise us.

sections.title: What it fetches
body: Public RSS/Atom feeds and sitemaps, and — only where your robots.txt allows it — public pages. It never signs in, never bypasses a paywall and never fetches private areas.
The crawler does not post comments, submit forms, send direct messages or email publishers automatically. A robots.txt rule is a crawl preference, not a content licence.

sections.title: What we keep
body: A headline, the link, the publication time and an excerpt of at most 200 characters. We do not store full article text or images. Every result shown to a customer links back to your original page.
Stored results follow each customer organization's retention settings. A publisher can request removal of stored results using the form below.

sections.title: How often
body: Publisher RSS/Atom feeds, sitemaps and allowed pages are normally checked every two hours. Optional Google Trends country feeds are checked at most every 15 minutes. Conditional requests avoid downloading unchanged feeds; errors and rate limits delay the next attempt.

sections.title: Opting out
body: Any of these works:
1) Send a takedown request with the form linked below — we block your domain, stop crawling it and, if you ask, delete what we stored.
2) Add a rule that names our crawler to your robots.txt: User-agent: Mediaory-Bot / Disallow: /. We honour rules that name Mediaory-Bot for feeds, and all applicable rules for pages and sitemaps.
We aim to answer requests within two business days.

takedown.title: Takedown
takedown.lead: If you publish a site we index and want us to stop, tell us here. We will block the domain, stop crawling it and, on request, delete what we stored.
takedown.name: Your name
takedown.targetsHint: For example: example.com, or the full address of a page.
takedown.authority: I am authorized to make this request for the publisher named above.
takedown.doneBody: Thank you. We will review it and reply by email, normally within two business days.
takedown.error: We could not send your request. Please check the form and try again.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What personal data Mediaory processes, why and on what basis, who receives it, how long we keep it, and the rights you have under Turkey's data protection law (KVKK). Written in plain language.

controller.title: Data controller
controller.intro: This notice is given under Article 10 of Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK). For the account, billing-contact, usage and form data described below, the data controller is:
controller.customers: When a customer puts personal data into its workspace (for example colleagues' names in comments), the customer decides why and how it is used and Mediaory processes it on the customer's behalf; a data processing addendum is available on request. For public sources, see section 5.

sections.title: What personal data we process
body: The data depends on how you use Mediaory:
items: Account data: your name, e-mail address, job title, language and time-zone preferences, and a hashed password.
Organization and billing contact data: the organization you belong to and your role. If you add a billing profile, the company name, tax office, tax number, address and invoice e-mail you enter.
Workspace content you create: monitoring keywords and queries, alert rules, tags, comments, assignments, reports and exports, and your organization's settings.
Security and usage data: sign-in sessions, IP address and browser type, security and audit events, usage counters (for example how many keywords or reports you use) and error logs.
Connected accounts: if you connect a YouTube or X account we keep its access tokens (stored encrypted) and the account's public identifier, and read only what the connection allows.
Forms: what you type into the contact, takedown and data-request forms, including your name and e-mail address.
People named in public sources: see section 5.

sections.title: Why we process it, and on what legal basis
body: We do not sell personal data, we do not use it for advertising, and we do not use your workspace data to train AI models.
Under Article 5 of the KVKK we rely on these bases:
items: Creating and running your account and providing the service: performance of a contract (Art. 5/2-c).
Service e-mails such as verification, invitations, alerts, digests and weekly archive links: performance of a contract (Art. 5/2-c). We do not send marketing e-mail.
Keeping the service secure, preventing abuse and fixing errors: our legitimate interest, which does not override your rights (Art. 5/2-f).
Indexing public sources so customers can monitor media coverage: our and our customers' legitimate interest, with the data kept to the minimum described in section 5 (Art. 5/2-f).
Invoicing and accounting records: legal obligation (Art. 5/2-ç).
Answering your requests and complaints, and establishing, exercising or defending legal claims: Art. 5/2-e and 5/2-f.
Connecting a social account: your consent, which you can withdraw at any time by disconnecting it (Art. 5/1).

sections.title: How we collect it
items: Directly from you: when you register, use the service or write to us.
Automatically: cookies and similar technologies (section 12) and server and security logs when you use Mediaory.
From the platforms you connect, with your authorization.
From public sources — RSS and Atom feeds, sitemaps and public web pages — for the content described in section 5.

sections.title: Content from public sources
body: We index publicly available sources. For each story we keep the headline, the link, the publication time, a public author name where the source gives one, and an excerpt of at most 200 characters; we do not keep the full text or images. For matching we also keep a word fingerprint: hashes of the words of the headline and summary, which cannot be turned back into text.

Press reports can contain sensitive information about the people they name. We do not build profiles of those people. Stories that no customer's monitoring matched are deleted after 14 days. Stories that were matched stay as mentions in the customer's workspace until the customer's own retention setting removes them or the organization is deleted, and are listed in the customer's weekly archive.

People named in public news are not our customers. If you want a story about you removed from our index, or have a question about it, send us its link (section 10); publishers can use the takedown form.

sections.title: Who receives it
body: We share personal data only with these groups:
items: Our service providers, who process it on our instructions: cloud hosting and database, object storage for archives, e-mail delivery, bot protection on public forms and — only if AI features are switched on — an AI provider. Each one, with its purpose and data, is listed on the service providers page.
The platforms you connect (Google/YouTube, X): data is exchanged only for that connection.
Other members of your organization, who see your name, e-mail address, role and the content you create in the workspace.
Authorities, courts and professional advisers, when the law requires or to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

sections.title: Transfers abroad
body: The service providers that help us run Mediaory are located outside Türkiye, mainly in the United States and the European Union, so personal data is transferred abroad when you use the service. Since the 2024 amendment of Article 9 of the KVKK, routine transfers abroad rest on the safeguards the law lists — an adequacy decision, the Board's standard contract, binding corporate rules or an approved undertaking — and no longer on explicit consent alone. Our transfers are made in line with Article 9.
You can ask us which safeguard applies to a given provider (section 10).

sections.title: How long we keep it
items: Account data: while your account exists. When you delete your account, your name, e-mail address and other personal details are irreversibly anonymized and your sessions are closed.
Organization data: when an organization is deleted its members lose access at once, and everything linked to it — mentions, reports, comments, archive files — is permanently erased after 30 days.
Stories that no monitoring matched: deleted after 14 days. Matched stories stay as mentions until the organization's retention setting removes them or the organization is deleted.
Sign-in sessions and one-time tokens (verification, password reset, invitations): removed 30 days after they expire or are used.
Billing and accounting records: for the period the law requires.
Contact, takedown and data-request forms: as long as needed to handle the request and to show how we answered it.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Under Article 11 of the KVKK you have the right to:
items: learn whether your personal data is processed;
request information if it has been processed;
learn the purpose of processing and whether it is used accordingly;
know the third parties it is transferred to, in Türkiye or abroad;
ask for correction if it is incomplete or inaccurate, and for the correction to be notified to those it was transferred to;
ask for deletion, destruction or anonymization when the reasons for processing no longer exist (Art. 7), and for that to be notified to those it was transferred to;
object to a result against you that arises solely from automated analysis; and
claim compensation for loss caused by unlawful processing.

sections.title: How to use your rights
body: Write to hello@mediaory.io, or to the address or KEP address in section 1. Tell us who you are and what you ask; we may ask for information to confirm your identity so that your data is not given to someone else.
We answer as soon as possible and within 30 days at the latest, free of charge. If answering needs extra cost, the fee set by the Personal Data Protection Board may be charged.
If you are a customer, you can export your account data and delete your account or organization yourself in Settings.
If you are not satisfied with our answer, or do not receive one in time, you can complain to the Personal Data Protection Board (kvkk.gov.tr).

sections.title: Security
body: We take technical and organizational measures proportionate to the risk, including:
items: encrypted connections (HTTPS) between your browser and Mediaory;
passwords stored only as salted hashes;
sign-in sessions that are signed, checked on the server and revocable;
access tokens of connected accounts stored encrypted;
role-based access, and a check on every request that the data belongs to your organization; and
an audit trail of sensitive actions, and rate limiting against abuse.
after: No system is perfectly secure. If a breach affects your personal data, we will notify the Personal Data Protection Board and the people affected as the law requires.

sections.title: Cookies
body: Mediaory uses only the cookies it needs to sign you in and to remember your language and theme. We use no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies. Details are on the cookie policy page.

sections.title: Changes to this notice
body: We update this notice when our processing changes. The date at the top shows the latest version, and we will tell account holders about material changes by e-mail or in the app.

sections.title: Contact
body: Privacy questions and requests: hello@mediaory.io. Publishers: use the takedown request form.

cookies.title: Cookie
cookies.lead: Which cookies and similar technologies Mediaory uses, why, and how to control them. In short: only what is needed to keep you signed in and to remember your choices — no analytics, no advertising, no tracking.

sections.title: What cookies are
body: Cookies are small text files a website stores in your browser. Similar technologies, such as your browser's local storage, serve the same purposes. On this page we call all of them cookies.

sections.title: Cookies we use
items: cim_session — keeps you signed in. Strictly necessary. Set when you sign in; removed when you sign out or after at most 30 days. It holds a signed identifier, not your data.
NEXT_LOCALE — remembers the language you chose. Functional. Kept for 1 year.
mediaory-panel-theme (your browser's local storage, not a cookie) — remembers light or dark mode in the app. Functional. Stays until you clear it.

sections.title: Cookies we do not use
body: We do not use analytics, advertising or tracking cookies, and we do not share cookie data with advertisers.

sections.title: Third parties
body: Where bot protection is switched on, the sign-up, password-reset and takedown forms load Cloudflare Turnstile, which may process technical signals from your browser to tell people from bots. Cloudflare acts as our service provider; see the service providers page.

sections.title: Legal basis and consent
body: Strictly necessary and functional cookies are used to provide the service you asked for and on the basis of our legitimate interest (KVKK Art. 5/2-c and 5/2-f), so no consent banner is needed. If we ever add analytics or other optional cookies, we will ask for your consent first.

sections.title: Managing cookies
body: You can delete or block cookies in your browser settings. If you block the session cookie you cannot sign in; if you block the language cookie we fall back to your browser's language.

sections.title: Contact
body: Questions: hello@mediaory.io. For everything about how we handle personal data, see the Privacy Notice.
